title: Data backend for fusionACS platform
text: purpose fusionACS project statistically fuse variables “donor” surveys (e.g., RECS, AHS) onto American Community Survey (ACS). Fusing donor variables onto ACS respondents creates large-sample, probabilistic simulations ACS respondents answered donor questionnaires. data science platform relies three core mechanisms: Shared Predictors: Common socioeconomic, demographic, housing attributes across donor surveys ACS. Gradient Boosting Models: Probabilistic simulation via variable-kk, conditional expectation matching using high-performance, gradient boosting machine learning models. title: Generate Output Files Resulting from Fusion — fusionOutput
text: fusionOutput() ties together machine-learning pipeline provided fusionModel package. Given valid setup created fusionInput, fusionOutput() manages complete modeling lifecycle: Data Assembly: Loads harmonized donor predictors, donor target variables (fusion_vars), spatial predictor variables matching donor's survey vintage geographic boundaries (PUMA 2010 vs. PUMA 2020). Predictor Selection (prepXY): Evaluates feature correlations screening thresholds via prepXY (reuses structure existing .fsn file fsn specified). Model Training (train): Trains gradient boosted decision trees via LightGBM using sensible default hyperparameters tuned production rapid test runs. Validation Fusing (fuse): validation = TRUE, fuses target variables back onto training data create validation dataset (.fsd) downstream evaluation. Recipient Prediction (fuse): Loads ACS microdata, merges spatial context predictors, fuses M implicates target variables onto recipient microdata.

title: Create Harmonized Microdata Datasets — harmonize
text: `harmonize()` executes variable transformation aggregation definitions recorded harmony file processed donor ACS microdata (`survey-processed/*.fst`). Key internal processing steps include: * **Microdata Loading:** Dynamically pulls matching household (`H`) person (`P`) `.fst`   files based harmony file specifications. * **Variable Transformation & Recoding:** Evaluates custom inline expressions (`adj`),   applies categorical grouping (`groups` / `levels`), assigns numeric break intervals   (`breaks`). * **Cross-Level Aggregation & Rescaling:** Automatically converts person-level variables   household-level (via methods reference person assignment, mean, min, max)   replicates household attributes across person-level observations required   `respondent` level. * **Geographic Attribute Retention:** Automatically extracts state PUMA geographic   identifiers recipient ACS observations across vintages.

text: comparison uses grid 1,000 quantiles evaluated via fquantile. Quantile differences weighted using Gaussian kernel centered median (\(p = 0.5\), \(\sigma = 0.15\)) emphasize central distributional overlap deemphasizing extreme tail behavior. score calculated normalized relative distance subtracted 1: $$\text{Similarity} = 1 - \frac{\sum w_i |q_{x,} - q_{y,}|}{\sum w_i \frac{|q_{x,}| + |q_{y,}|}{2}}$$

title: Process ACS PUMS Microdata, Codebooks, and Custom Variables — processACScodebook
text: processACScodebook Mechanics: Census Bureau distributes PUMS data dictionaries different file formats depending vintage: Pre-2012: Distributed primarily raw unformatted .pdf files. 2012–2016: Distributed fixed-width / structured .txt files. 2017 Onward: Distributed structured .csv files. processACScodebook() abstracts format differences unified output table, identifying value ranges, applying human-readable level descriptions, flagging variables subject inflation adjustment factors (ADJINC ADJHSG). processACScustom Mechanics & Script Requirements: Standard PUMS microdata often lacks domain-specific recoded metrics required downstream modeling (e.g., custom poverty ratios, recoded race/ethnicity categories, housing cost burdens). processACScustom() automates execution validation derived variables: Script Scanning: Scans survey-processed/ACS/custom/*.R individual R scripts. Function Contract: custom script must define function named identically filename (e.g., poverty.R defines poverty()). function must accept year sole argument return data frame containing primary keys (hid, optionally pid). Validation Checks: Guarantees zero missing (NA) values exist output columns, verifies explicit variable labels assigned via var_label, filters records occupied housing units, prevents column name collisions across scripts. Typical Execution Workflow: Primary Microdata Build (processACSmicrodata): raw Census ZIP archives (csv_hus.zip csv_pus.zip) placed survey-raw/ACS/{year}/, standard operating procedure call processACSmicrodata() respondent units given vintage: orchestrates key standardization, financial inflation adjustments, geographic filtering, codebook label mapping, non-response imputation via fusionModel, binary output generation. Internal Codebook Parsing (processACScodebook): function called internally processACSmicrodata() automatically locate parse vintage-dependent data dictionary files (.pdf, .txt, .csv). Users generally need invoke processACScodebook() separately, except debugging dictionary parsing discrepancies testing raw Census codebook structures. Custom Variable Compilation (processACScustom): processACSmicrodata() executed successfully household (H) person (P) records, processACScustom() can executed: dynamically scans, validates, evaluates user-defined transformation scripts survey-processed/ACS/custom/*.R, appending custom metrics standalone sidecar files updating primary metadata dictionary.
